6. Assay Protocol
A. Reagent Preparation
1. Hydrolysis Enzyme Mix:
Reconstitute with 220 µl Glycogen Hydrolysis Buffer. Pipette up and down to dissolve completely. Aliquot and store at -20°C. Avoid repeated freeze/thaw. Keep on ice while in use. Use within two months.
2. Development Enzyme Mix:
Reconstitute with 220 µl ddH2O. Pipette up and down to dissolve completely. Aliquot and store at -20°C. Keep on ice while in use. Use within two months.
3. Probe:
Reconstitute with 220 µl dH2O. Pipette up and down to dissolve completely. Stable for 2 months at -20°C.

steps.title: Prepare reagents
steps.instruction: Store the kit at -20 °C, protect from light and avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles. Warm Glycogen Hydrolysis Buffer and Glycogen Development Buffer to room temperature before use. Briefly centrifuge all small vials prior to opening.

steps.title: Generate standard curve
steps.instruction: Dilute the 2 mg ml⁻¹ Glycogen Standard to 0.2 mg ml⁻¹ (0.2 µg µl⁻¹) by mixing 10 µl of the stock with 90 µl dH₂O and mix well. Pipette 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 µl of this dilution into separate wells of a 96‑well plate, giving 0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2, 1.6 and 2 µg glycogen per well. Adjust each well to a final volume of 50 µl with Glycogen Hydrolysis Buffer.

steps.title: Prepare samples
steps.instruction: Homogenize 10 mg tissue or 1 × 10⁶ cells in 200 µl ddH₂O for 10 min on ice. Boil the homogenate for 10 min to inactivate enzymes, then centrifuge at 18 000 rpm for 10 min. Transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube; it is ready for assay. Pipette 1–50 µl of the supernatant (≈50 µg protein) into a well and bring the volume to 50 µl with Glycogen Hydrolysis Buffer.

steps.title: Hydrolyze glycogen
steps.instruction: Add 2 µl Hydrolysis Enzyme Mix to each standard and sample well, mix well, and incubate at room temperature for 30 min. Do not add Hydrolysis Enzyme Mix to background‑control wells.

steps.title: Prepare reaction mix
steps.instruction: For each well prepare a 50 µl reaction mixture. For standard/sample wells combine 44 µl Glycogen Development Buffer, 2 µl Development Enzyme Mix and 2 µl Probe. For background‑control wells combine 46 µl Glycogen Development Buffer, 2 µl Development Enzyme Mix and 2 µl Probe. Add 48 µl of the appropriate reaction mix to each standard or sample well (which already contains 2 µl Hydrolysis Enzyme Mix) and add 50 µl of the background‑control mix to background wells.

steps.title: Incubate and read
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 30 min, then measure absorbance at 450 nm using a microplate reader.

steps.title: Analyze data
steps.instruction: Subtract the 0 µg glycogen standard reading from all wells. Plot the standard curve. If a background‑control reading is significant, subtract it from each sample reading. Use the corrected sample absorbance to obtain the glycogen amount B (µg) from the standard curve, then calculate sample concentration C = B ÷ V (where V is the sample volume added to the well, µl). Express results as µg glycogen per mg tissue or other desired units. Glycogen molecular weight is approximately 1 × 10⁵–1 × 10⁷ g mol⁻¹.

2 1. Overview
Glycogen serves as the main carbohydrate storage in animals and can be converted to glucose readily. It is primarily found in the liver and muscle tissues. Glycogen is a branched biopolymer comprising of α-1,4 linkage with α-1,6 linkages occurring every 8-10 glucose units along the backbone. Abnormal ability to utilize glycogen is found in diabetes and in several genetic glycogen storage diseases. Abcam’s Glycogen Assay Kit II (Colorimetric) (ab169558) provides a simple, fast and robust way to measure Glycogen levels in various biological samples. This assay is suitable for measuring Glycogen levels in samples that contain reducing substances, which may interfere with the oxidase-based assays. In this assay, Glycogen is hydrolyzed into glucose, which is oxidized to form an intermediate that reduces a colorless probe to a colored product with strong absorbance at 450 nm. This high-throughput suitable assay kit can detect less than 4 µg/ml of Glycogen in samples.
